items.title: Doug Carn interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2023
items.q: my mom had a bunch of books, poetry books by Yeats and Keats and different people. And you know I’ve read those you know.

ctx.x: Wonderful. The music that you were playing at that time at some point did you decide instead of going down this pop music road I have something I want to say in the jazz world?

Right because this is the thing, I had said all of that through high school, like “It’s Just the Nearness of You” you know. But the substance of the song and the lyrics is the same as some of these R&B songs. Baby let me get close to you, you know? I mean and it’s romantic you know. It’s just on a higher level. But the problem was I wanted to play you know. I just didn’t want to play songs you know. So I said well maybe I’ll write some songs the way that I would like to play them you know, the type that I would…
“How High the Moon” and all of them songs was old tunes then. You know? “Satin Doll” was an old song in 1962 you know?
